litigation.mdlName: In re: Suboxone (Buprenorphine/Naloxone) Film Products Liability Litigation
litigation.court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of Ohio (Cleveland)

phaseDetail: The July 16, 2026 CMO 23 governs provider depositions in the core discovery pool. The Second Amended CMO 15 schedules core-pool depositions through January 15, 2027 and trial-pool selection for January 29. Its later timetable describes March 2028 as a proposed first trial setting, not a fixed trial date.

settlements.label: No global injury settlement announced in records reviewed
settlements.detail: The Northern District of Ohio public MDL order index and bellwether protocol reviewed September 14, 2026 do not announce a dental-injury settlement program or individual payout schedule. Separate Suboxone antitrust and opioid-enforcement settlements do not resolve these dental-injury claims.

keyDates.label: MDL-3092 established
keyDates.detail: JPML centralized federal Suboxone dental-injury cases before Judge J. Philip Calabrese in the Northern District of Ohio.

keyDates.label: CMO No. 4 — mass-filing (Schedule A) procedure
keyDates.detail: The court authorized a master 'Schedule A' filing covering thousands of claimants, with severed plaintiffs later required to file individual actions.

keyDates.label: Second Amended CMO No. 15 — bellwether protocol
keyDates.detail: Set the core-discovery-pool schedule for bellwether selection.

keyDates.label: Random selection of 20 core-discovery cases (scheduled)
keyDates.detail: The court's random selection of the first 20 cases for the 50-case core discovery pool was scheduled for June 10, 2026 under the Second Amended CMO No. 15 bellwether protocol.

keyDates.label: CMO 23 provider-deposition protocol
keyDates.detail: Order governs provider depositions in the core discovery pool.

keyDates.label: Core discovery deposition period ends
keyDates.detail: Scheduled end of core-pool depositions under Second Amended CMO 15.

keyDates.label: Trial-pool case selection
keyDates.detail: Protocol schedules selection of 15 trial-pool cases.
